mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has fallen for three consecutive weeks (0.4 -> 1.3 -> -0.6 -> -2.7). This downward momentum reflects accumulating behavioral inertia (habit formation around reduced outings) that persists without a reversing shock, so the next four weeks should continue trending lower before stabilizing.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC declined monotonically across the last three weekly means
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days exceeds the last 28-day mean despite three prior weeks of decline, the momentum mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp week-on-week surge in GROCERY_PHARM (3.3 -> 10.3 -> 11.4) indicates stockpiling and consolidation of errands into essential-only trips, substituting away from discretionary retail and recreation visits for the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises more than 7 points week-on-week while RETAIL_REC falls in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose from 3.3 to 11.4 over two weeks while RETAIL_REC fell
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rebounds upward within two weeks despite continued elevated GROCERY_PHARM levels above 10, the substitution hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in TRANSIT (9.1 -> -3.0) and softening WORKPLACES (11.9 -> 9.7) jointly signal an emerging restriction regime on commuting and work-based travel; their combined contraction removes incidental foot traffic that normally feeds retail and recreation visits, compounding the drop over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES decline in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT turned negative in the most recent week while WORKPLACES declined for the first time
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC stabilizes or rises over the next four weeks even as TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both continue to contract, the joint-decline mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Under a tightening-restrictions regime, a collapse in PARKS (5.0 -> -16.4 -> -12.1) alongside a rising RESIDENTIAL trend (-2.0 -> -0.4 -> 0.0) indicates enforced sheltering-in-place; this suppresses all non-essential outdoor and retail movement, driving RETAIL_REC lower over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS dropped sharply while RESIDENTIAL rose toward zero and beyond baseline
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not decline further while PARKS remains deeply negative and RESIDENTIAL keeps rising, the sheltering mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL crossing from negative into zero/positive territory (-2.0 -> -0.4 -> 0.0) marks a tipping point where households shift time allocation fully toward home-based activity, producing an immediate one-week drop in RETAIL_REC as discretionary trips are curtailed.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL crosses above 0 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL reached 0.0 at t-0w after being negative for three prior weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not fall in the week immediately following RESIDENTIAL crossing zero, the tipping-point hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-March typically brings seasonal warming that would normally lift PARKS and outdoor-adjacent retail activity; absent that seasonal uplift becoming visible in PARKS despite the calendar date, RETAIL_REC fails to receive its usual spring boost and instead continues a flat-to-negative trajectory over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell to -12.1 at t-0w despite early-spring timing
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises over the next four weeks alongside continued seasonal PARKS weakness, the seasonal-suppression hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction of rising GROCERY_PHARM (essential-trip concentration) and rising RESIDENTIAL (home-dwelling) signals a joint behavioral shift toward minimizing non-essential outings; together these two trends reinforce each other to depress RETAIL_REC more than either alone would predict over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM above 10 and RESIDENTIAL at or above 0 in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM reached 11.4 while RESIDENTIAL reached 0.0 in the same week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises over the next two weeks despite both GROCERY_PHARM staying above 10 and RESIDENTIAL staying at or above 0, the joint behavioral-shift hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week TRANSIT drop exceeding 10 points (from 3.0 to -3.0) indicates a sudden policy-driven or fear-driven collapse in public transit use, which mechanically removes a key access channel to retail districts and causes an immediate one-week contraction in RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 10 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell from 3.0 to -3.0 between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not decline in the week immediately following a TRANSIT drop exceeding 10 points, the transit-access mechanism is rejected.
